text:
KNOWS ME: a lot

MOMENT 1:
What happened: A relative was in hospital during a week when work was already busy.
What you did or said: You organised the visiting rota, handled insurance calls, and kept going to work.
Your words: If I fall apart, everyone falls apart, so I don't get to.
Area: family

MOMENT 2:
What happened: A sister offered to take a week away from work to share the hospital tasks.
What you did or said: You thanked her, declined the offer, and continued arranging everything yourself.
Your words: It's easier if I just do it myself.
Area: relationships

MOMENT 3:
What happened: A quiet Sunday followed a sixty-hour work week.
What you did or said: You felt guilty while resting and looked for something productive to finish.
Your words: I'm only good when I'm getting things done.
Area: work

MOMENT 4:
What happened: A manager praised your work on a hospital-ward handover project.
What you did or said: You brushed off the praise and treated the result as ordinary.
Your words: Anyone could have done it, I just had the time.
Area: work

MOMENT 5:
What happened: A small spreadsheet error was sent to a manager and caused no visible problem.
What you did or said: You replayed it through the night and worried that it changed how people saw all your work.
Your words: One mistake and people start to wonder what else you've got wrong.
Area: work

MOMENT 6:
What happened: Friends met for the book group you describe as the best part of the week.
What you did or said: You did not tell them how hard the previous months had been.
Your words: They've got their own stuff, I don't want to be a burden.
Area: relationships

MOMENT 7:
What happened: A friend suggested a holiday after your emergency savings reached its target.
What you did or said: You delayed the trip until the fund reached a newer, higher number.
Your words: I know it's fine, but I need to see it's fine.
Area: money

MOMENT 8:
What happened: A supplier report included numbers you believed were padded.
What you did or said: You refused to sign it even though the meeting became awkward.
Your words: I'd rather be the difficult one than the one who lied.
Area: morality

THEME 1: Being useful and dependable often seems connected to feeling that you belong.
Seen: 4

THEME 2: Other people are treated as kind, while needing their kindness is treated as risky.
Seen: 2

THEME 3: Safety is checked through work completed, errors avoided, and money kept visible.
Seen: 3

THEME 4: A time it went the other way was refusing a padded report even when agreement would have been easier.
Seen: 2

RULE 1: Keep everything moving before you allow yourself to rest.
Seen: 4

RULE 2: Do not ask other people to carry what you can carry yourself.
Seen: 3

RULE 3: One preventable mistake can put earlier trust at risk.
Seen: 2

PATTERN 1: Taking over practical work when uncertainty or need appears.
Seen: 4

PATTERN 2: Redirecting praise and keeping difficulty private.
Seen: 3

PATTERN 3: Moving the safety target after reaching it.
Seen: 2

MATTERS 1: Reliability and care for close people.
Seen: 4

MATTERS 2: Honesty even when it makes a group moment uncomfortable.
Seen: 2

MATTERS 3: Enough financial room that a sudden problem does not become a crisis.
Seen: 3

KNOWS ME: some

MOMENT 1:
What happened: A payment-retry pull request was approved without comments.
What you did or said: You treated the approval as evidence that nobody had reviewed the work carefully.
Your words: Nobody really read it.
Area: work

MOMENT 2:
What happened: A team lead selected you to mentor a new developer.
What you did or said: You assumed the choice reflected a shortage of alternatives rather than trust in you.
Your words: She must have run out of options.
Area: work

MOMENT 3:
What happened: A weekend began after you had not cleared every item from the work board.
What you did or said: You kept working and found it hard to enjoy the open time.
Your words: If I take a nap I feel like I owe the day an apology.
Area: work

MOMENT 4:
What happened: A colleague received public credit for work completed by several people.
What you did or said: You stayed angry because the whole group had not been credited fairly.
Your words: It's not even about me, it's that it wasn't fair to the whole team.
Area: morality

MOMENT 5:
What happened: A partner was already stressed when something in the relationship upset you.
What you did or said: You kept the upset to yourself and hoped the partner would notice without being asked.
Your words: Sometimes I wish he'd just notice without me having to say it.
Area: relationships

MOMENT 6:
What happened: A difficult technical problem arrived during a stressful period.
What you did or said: You went deeper into debugging because the bounded problem quieted everything else.
Your words: The one place where my brain goes quiet.
Area: work

MOMENT 7:
What happened: Parents asked about salary and title during a family conversation.
What you did or said: You left out the difficult parts of work so they would not worry.
Your words: It just worries them and then it's my fault for worrying them.
Area: family

MOMENT 8:
What happened: You imagined where close friends might be in five years and then considered your own future.
What you did or said: You pictured good things for them but described your future as unchanged and more tiring.
Your words: Probably the same, just more tired.
Area: meaning

THEME 1: Good outcomes are often explained as luck while difficult outcomes are treated as proof.
Seen: 3

THEME 2: Rest and enjoyment can seem to require a completed task as justification.
Seen: 3

THEME 3: Needs are kept small even when being noticed and understood matters.
Seen: 2

THEME 4: A time it went the other way was speaking up when a whole team was denied fair credit.
Seen: 2

RULE 1: Clear the work before taking time that is only for you.
Seen: 3

RULE 2: Do not add your needs when someone close is already carrying stress.
Seen: 2

RULE 3: Apply the same rules to everyone, including people with status or connections.
Seen: 3

PATTERN 1: Discounting praise, selection, or approval as weak evidence.
Seen: 3

PATTERN 2: Turning free time into another technical project.
Seen: 3

PATTERN 3: Going quiet about needs and hoping a close person notices them.
Seen: 2

MATTERS 1: Fair rules and shared credit.
Seen: 4

MATTERS 2: Learning through useful technical work.
Seen: 3

MATTERS 3: Being understood without costing another person too much.
Seen: 2

KNOWS ME: some

MOMENT 1:
What happened: A good freelance income month was followed by a quieter week.
What you did or said: You treated the quiet week as the possible start of losing financial steadiness.
Your words: I've had good years, but I've never had a safe year.
Area: money

MOMENT 2:
What happened: A client invoice remained unpaid for sixty days.
What you did or said: You avoided another reminder because asking again felt more exposing than losing the fee.
Your words: I'd rather eat the cost than send another reminder and look desperate.
Area: money

MOMENT 3:
What happened: Back pain made an ordinary desk chair difficult to keep using.
What you did or said: You bought a better chair only after describing it as required for work.
Your words: If it's for work it's fine. If it's for me it's indulgent.
Area: body

MOMENT 4:
What happened: A client rejected one logo concept during a normal review.
What you did or said: You experienced the response as a judgement of your taste and identity.
Your words: It feels like they rejected my taste, which is basically me.
Area: work

MOMENT 5:
What happened: An agency offered a secure full-time role after a period of freelance uncertainty.
What you did or said: You declined because being managed felt more costly than losing predictable income.
Your words: I'd rather be broke and free than comfortable and owned.
Area: work

MOMENT 6:
What happened: Friends could have helped when you moved to a new flat.
What you did or said: You hired movers instead of asking because accepting help could create an unspoken debt.
Your words: People say yes and then resent you.
Area: relationships

MOMENT 7:
What happened: A close friend offered to review a portfolio site.
What you did or said: You thanked the friend but never sent the link.
Your words: I don't like owing people.
Area: relationships

MOMENT 8:
What happened: A close friend's car failed four hours away late at night.
What you did or said: You drove there immediately and treated showing up as obvious.
Your words: If you're mine, you're mine.
Area: relationships

THEME 1: Dependence can feel dangerous whether it involves clients, employers, or friends.
Seen: 4

THEME 2: Spending and asking are easier when they can be justified as work rather than personal need.
Seen: 3

THEME 3: Creative feedback can land as a judgement of the whole person rather than one piece of work.
Seen: 2

THEME 4: A time it went the other way was driving through the night when a close friend needed practical help.
Seen: 2

RULE 1: Keep enough independence that no one else can decide the terms of your life.
Seen: 4

RULE 2: Do not owe other people help that they might later resent giving.
Seen: 3

RULE 3: Personal spending needs a practical reason before it is allowed.
Seen: 2

PATTERN 1: Underquoting or delaying invoice reminders to avoid looking needy.
Seen: 3

PATTERN 2: Refusing offered help while giving immediate help to close people.
Seen: 3

PATTERN 3: Continuing to refine work after the client already considers it complete.
Seen: 2

MATTERS 1: Freedom to choose how and for whom you work.
Seen: 4

MATTERS 2: Loyalty expressed by showing up when it is inconvenient.
Seen: 3

MATTERS 3: Beauty and care in ordinary creative details.
Seen: 2
